summary: John Clifford Holt is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Gustavus Adolphus College, the Graduate Theological Union, and the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah. He was a longtime professor at Bowdoin College (1978–2019).
John Cockburn Thomson (1834–1860) was an Indologist. He earned his B.A. at Trinity College, Oxford (1852–1857), studying under Horace Hayman Wilson and Christian Lassen.

John Collinson Nesfield (1836–1919) worked in linguistics and Indology after studying at Highgate School and Merton College, Oxford. He served as a professor at Presidency University and Krishnagar Government College, and later as principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
John Correia-Afonso (1924–2005) was an historian and archaeologist. He studied under Henry Heras from around 1949 to 1953 and later succeeded him.

John Corrigan is a religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (~1978–1982). He held posts at the University of Virginia and Arizona State University before becoming Chair of the Department of Religion at Florida State University.

John Crawfurd (1783–1868) worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He completed an M.D. at the University of Edinburgh (~1800–1803), served as a physician for the East India Company (1803–1808), and succeeded Stamford Raffles in 1823.
John Cripps Pembrey (1832–1916) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He held the post of Oriental Reader at Clarendon Press, attested in 1904 and 1916.

John Cumming (1868–1958) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Glasgow and Balliol College, Oxford, and served as Vice-Chairman at SOAS University of London from 1925 to 1946.
John D'Oyly (1774–1824) was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He was educated at the University of Cambridge, completing his B.A. at Corpus Christi College between 1792 and 1796.

John D. Dunne specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. Educated at Amherst College and Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Malcolm David Eckel, he taught at Emory University and holds a distinguished professorship at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.
John D. Kelly is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He holds a post at the University of Chicago, serving as the Christian W. Mackauer Professor of Anthropology and of Social Sciences.

John D. Smith is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as a Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London in 1975 before joining the University of Cambridge, where he was Lecturer and later Professor (2001–2007).

John Daido Loori (1931–2009) was a Buddhist practitioner and teacher who studied under Soen Nakagawa and Taizan Maezumi. He served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery (~1980–2009) and founded the Mountains and Rivers Order.
John Daishin Buksbazen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles under teachers Taizan Maezumi and Bernie Glassman.

John David Paterson (1754–1809) worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He served in the East India Company from 1776, worked as a judge and magistrate at the University of Dhaka, and founded The Asiatic Society.

John David Rees (1854–1922) was an Indologist and civil servant educated at Cheltenham College. He served in the Madras Civil Service, the Indian Civil Service (~1875–1901), and as an Additional Member of the Council of India (1895–1900).

John Dawson Mayne (1828–1917) was an Indologist and legal scholar educated at Trinity College Dublin (~1845–1849). He served as Professor of Law at Presidency College, Chennai (~1857–1872), and Professor of Common Law at the Inns of Court (1880–1885).
John DeFrancis (1911–2009) was a sinologist and linguist who studied at Columbia and Yale. He taught at Seton Hall University (~1961–1966) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1966–1976).

John Dewey (1859–1952) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vermont and Johns Hopkins University. He held professorships at the universities of Michigan, Minnesota, Chicago (~1894–1904), and Columbia University (~1904–1930).

John Dowson (1820–1881) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history who studied under Edwin Norris. He was a tutor at East India Company College and served as Professor of Hindustani at University College London and Staff College, Camberley.
